name: Sony PlayStation Portable family
summary: Explore PSP family hardware and homebrew routes: ARK custom firmware installs from official 6.60/6.61 on every model, with CustomIPL for a permanent boot-time install.

specs.cpu: MIPS R4000-based at up to 333 MHz
specs.gpu: Custom GPU (MPEG-0/1/2 decoder, VU0/VU1 vector units)
specs.storage: Memory Stick Duo (Memory Stick Micro on the Go); 16 GB internal on the Go
specs.media: UMD drive (all except the PSP Go)

variants.storage: 16384 KB internal flash + Memory Stick Duo slot
variants.notes: Heavier; no TV output. Pandora Battery recovery is available on this model only.

variants.storage: Same flash as 1000 + Memory Stick Duo slot
variants.notes: Slimmer form factor; TV output added; more RAM.

variants.storage: Same flash as 2000 + Memory Stick Duo slot
variants.notes: Brighter screen; built-in microphone; same flash layout as 2000.

variants.storage: 16 GB internal storage; Memory Stick Micro slot
variants.notes: Slider design; no UMD drive; Bluetooth instead of Wi-Fi.
Budget model for Europe; mono speaker; no Wi-Fi.

homebrew.name: ARK-5 (via FasterARK)
homebrew.firmware: Official System Software 6.60 or 6.61 (6.60TT and 6.60DT also supported)
homebrew.summary: Next-generation custom firmware for PSP and Vita's ePSP. FasterARK installs from official 6.60/6.61 and provides the CFW plus plugin management, XMB integration, and overclocking.

compatibility.note: Upstream states official 6.60/6.61 (including TT and DT variants) are the install range; claims every retail PSP model.

requirements: PSP on official System Software 6.60 or 6.61; update if necessary via Sony's update.
A Memory Stick Duo (or Memory Stick Micro on the Go) with extracted FasterARK package.
warnings: ARK-4 is archived; use FasterARK/ARK-5 instead.
Fake or failing Memory Sticks are a common cause of failed installations.

homebrew.name: CustomIPL
homebrew.firmware: Every firmware; requires a prior ARK-5 install via FasterARK
homebrew.summary: Patches the IPL so the custom firmware loads on cold-boot, turning ARK into a permanent CFW instead of live CFW (which needs the loader after every power-off/reboot).

compatibility.note: Installed after FasterARK works; upstream states it allows CFW to be loaded from cold-boot on all retail models.

warnings: A failed CustomIPL install can require DC10 or a Pandora Battery recovery.

homebrew.name: DC10 (Despertar del Cementerio)
homebrew.firmware: Installs 6.61 with or without ARK; works on all retail models
homebrew.summary: ARK's ultimate recovery tool. It reinstalls 6.61 (with or without ARK), backs up and restores NAND and IDStorage, and can permanently change the UMD region. Requires a boot method to start.

compatibility.note: Shipped in the Full variant of FasterARK; upstream says it works on all retail PSP models.

requirements: The 6.61 firmware renamed to 661.PBP (or 661GO.PBP on a Go) on the Memory Stick.
A boot method: Pandora Battery (PSP-1000 only), Baryon Sweeper, or New cIPL with L held.
warnings: Not a universal unbrick by itself — requires one of the boot methods listed above.
Pandora Battery is only available on the PSP-1000.

homebrew.name: Pandora Battery (PSP-1000 only)
homebrew.summary: A modified battery that forces a PSP-1000 into service mode when paired with a magic Memory Stick, enabling DC10 access on a bricked console.

compatibility.note: Only works on PSP-1000; all other PSP models lack the service-mode entry path.

requirements: A modified battery prepared outside the console.
A magic Memory Stick with DC10.
warnings: Old batteries are 15+ years; a swollen battery is a safety hazard.

homebrew.name: Infinity (persistent CFW patch)
homebrew.firmware: Official System Software 6.60 or 6.61; the installer runs from the firmware update slot.
homebrew.summary: Installs persistent custom firmware on PSP 6.60/6.61 for every model, so ARK or PRO/ME starts at boot instead of being re-launched as an exploit.

compatibility.note: README: persistent custom firmware on 6.60 and 6.61 for every model, with separate standard and PSPgo packages.

requirements: A PSP on official firmware 6.60 or 6.61.
The matching Infinity package (standard or PSPgo).
A custom firmware such as ARK or PRO/ME to enable after installing Infinity.
warnings: Installing Infinity modifies the firmware; a failed or interrupted install can leave the console needing recovery.
Uninstall Infinity versions below 2.0 with Chronoswitch 7 or newer first.
homebrew.availability: Open source (MIT); releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: Chronoswitch Downgrader
homebrew.firmware: Runs from official or custom firmware; the README documents downgrading with the matching official update, for example to 6.60.
homebrew.summary: A signed downgrader for the PSP that installs an older official firmware from a memory stick or internal storage. It is also the documented way to uninstall old Infinity versions.

compatibility.note: README documents running the downgrader and flashing the matching official update; PSPgo needs the PSPgo firmware image.
README names the PSP and PSPgo; the Street/E1000 is not called out.

requirements: The official firmware update for the version you want to install, placed at PSP/GAME/UPDATE/EBOOT.PBP.
The correct model firmware image: PSPgo images only on PSPgo.
warnings: Downgrading flashes system software; an interrupted install or a wrong-model update can brick the console.
Use only the official update that matches the model.
homebrew.availability: Signed build; releases published by the project.
